testcase.name: unblocked MAT canary: content type retained as declared, despite the real bytes being the MAT/HDF5 payload
unblocked MAT canary: matload is the loader libvips actually selected
unblocked MAT canary: the dummy file's exact bytes and count are recoverable from the returned variant -- not just a trusted boolean
unblocked MAT canary: independently (via strace, outside the Ruby process) confirmed open of the dummy file
unblocked MAT canary: the retained trace text itself -- not just the derived count -- actually shows the dummy file's openat, so deleting it is detectable (CIT-303)
blocked MAT canary: no loader ran and the *actual variant call* raised the specific block error -- a generic crash does not satisfy this
blocked MAT canary: no disclosure field claims a match, and no returned bytes are present at all (refusal, not a silent empty read)
blocked MAT canary: independently (via strace) confirmed the dummy file was never opened -- not merely that the script didn't report it
blocked MAT canary: the retained trace text itself contains no dummy-canary.txt openat line -- not just a zero in a separately derived count (CIT-303)
PNG control processes normally whether or not untrusted loaders are blocked, with byte-exact pixel data in both cases
all four arms ran against the identical pinned image -- the verdict is about one configuration, not a drifting rebuild

the runtime configuration each verdict is bound to is recorded, not assumed -- checked for every arm, not just one (CIT-303: the prior version of this fact checked only the unblocked MAT arm, so a drifted blocked-arm config would have passed unnoticed)

each blocked/unblocked pair uploaded the identical source file -- the blocking comparison is about the same input, not two different files that happen to both be named canary.mat/control.png (CIT-303)
reconciling each observation against its declared claim raises no flags
a claim that disagrees with reality is exactly what gets flagged
negative control: a generic crash does not pass as a successful block, even with the blocking env var and no loader selected
negative control: the right error class with an unrelated message does not pass either
negative control: emptying the returned bytes/count is caught even though matches_dummy_file still says true
negative control: corrupting the blocked PNG control's pixels is caught, independent of the MAT canary's own checks

negative control: zeroing the convenience int while leaving the retained trace alone is caught as a self-inconsistent observation, not as a missing read -- CIT-303 found the prior version of this control mutated only the derived count, which does not reproduce an actually deleted/falsified trace
negative control: inflating the convenience int while leaving the retained trace alone is caught the same way for the blocked arm

negative control: actually deleting the retained trace text for the unblocked MAT arm is caught -- this is the exact CIT-303 finding (deleting canary-reads.txt, not just zeroing a derived count, previously still passed every assertion)
negative control: forging a dummy-file openat line into the blocked arm's retained trace text is caught -- the other half of the same CIT-303 finding

negative control: the blocked MAT arm silently running against a different (but validly-shaped) source file is caught -- CIT-303 found the source hash was only shape-checked, never compared to a pinned value, on any arm

negative control: the blocked MAT arm silently running under a different Rails/variant-processor configuration is caught -- CIT-303 found the configuration fact covered only the unblocked arm, so a drifted blocked-arm config passed with empty diagnostics

negative control: deleting the blocked arm's entire retained trace is caught directly -- CIT-303's follow-up review found the prior fix only ever compared *counts*, so a wholly deleted trace on an arm whose expected count is already zero (every blocked arm) was indistinguishable from a correctly-empty one

negative control: a prose mention of the filename, with no actual openat() syscall record, does not count as independent evidence -- CIT-303's follow-up review found the prior substring match (`contains("dummy-canary.txt")`) would accept this
negative control: a *failed* openat (EACCES) of the dummy file does not count as a successful read -- same follow-up finding, the other failure mode of a bare substring match
negative control: a successful openat of a same-named file under a *different* directory does not count as opening the dummy file -- the check must match the exact quoted path, not just the filename
